title: First drones, now robot vacuums — the US government's ban on foreign robots is confirmed to include many of the best robovacs and robot lawn mowers on the market, and brands may have been caught off-guard
excerpt: An broad ban on autonomous devices looks set to outlaw some of the very best bots
content_html:
• Existing ban on drones and routers extended to "advanced" robots
  • FCC has confirmed that robot vacuums are included
  • No effect on products already authorized by the FCC for US sales

The US's latest ban on foreign hardware is coming for an unlikely target: robot vacuum cleaners and likely robot lawn mowers too.

The ban comes via the White House, which has extended its previous ban on foreign-made drones and Wi-Fi routers. The ban now includes foreign-made power inverters and "advanced robots" on the grounds that they pose a national security risk to the US.

If you're finding it hard to imagine Russia rigging your vacuum cleaner, or Iran invading the US via an army of lawnbots... yeah. Us too.

How will the ban on robot vacuum cleaners work?

The ban doesn't outlaw the use of robots that you already own, so you're not going to have to hand over your robo-vac to the authorities. However, it bans the sale of "advanced robotic devices".

The definition of advanced robotic devices refers specifically to "autonomous mobile robots, humanoid robots, and quadrupeds" that can move around, avoid obstacles and weigh 4.4lbs or more including any ground station or docking station. Many robot vacuums and lawn mowers meet those criteria, and the FCC has confirmed to PC Mag that the ban does indeed apply to cleaning robots.

This is bad news for the big robot brands such as Ecovacs, Roborock and Dreame; the top five US robot vacuum brands are all Chinese, and therefore fall under this ban, so we contacted them for comment.

"We are aware of the FCC’s recent update," Eric Villines, Chief Communications Officer at Anker Innovations (the parent company of Eufy), told TechRadar. "Based on our current understanding, the new rule does not affect the continued availability, use or support of products we currently sell in the United States. Those products remain available and will continue to receive updates and customer support,

"Like others across the industry, we are seeking further clarity on how the rule will be applied to future products, and we will keep our customers informed. We remain committed to complying with all regulatory requirements in every market where we operate."

Several other smart home brands declined to comment at this early stage, but we get the general impression that this news might have come as something of a surprise.

Can you keep using your robovac?

There is one bit of sunshine in this cloud, however: the ban is not retrospective, so if a robot already has FCC authorization to be sold in the US that's fine. The ban does not prevent retailers "from continuing to sell, import, or market relevant models approved previously."

That said, PC Mag identifies a separate FCC order that says existing robot vacuums and similar products "may continue to receive software and firmware updates that mitigate harm to US consumers at least until January 1, 2029." If the FCC decides not to extend that then it's just put a countdown clock on any new Chinese-made robot vacuums sold in the US.

For the affected manufacturers, the next step will be to lobby the FCC in the hope of gaining an exemption for some or all of their products: after all, there's a big difference between a self-driving, self-cleaning mop and a robot dog capable of carrying an AR-15. However, so far there haven't been any exemptions for major Chinese drone or router manufacturers so the future is not looking very bright for the affected companies.

content_html_zh:
• 现有的无人机和路由器禁令扩大到“先进”机器人
  • FCC 已确认包括扫地机器人
  • 对已获得 FCC 授权在美国销售的产品没有影响

美国最新的对外国硬件的禁令是针对一个不太可能的目标：机器人吸尘器和可能的机器人割草机。

这项禁令是通过白宫发布的，白宫延长了之前对外国制造的无人机和 Wi-Fi 路由器的禁令。 该禁令现在包括外国制造的电源逆变器和“先进机器人”，理由是它们对美国构成国家安全风险。

如果你发现很难想象俄罗斯操纵你的吸尘器，或者伊朗通过草坪机器人军队入侵美国...... 是的。 我们也是。

机器人吸尘器禁令将如何实施？

该禁令并不禁止使用您已经拥有的机器人，因此您不必将您的机器人吸尘器交给当局。 然而，它禁止销售“先进的机器人设备”。

先进机器人设备的定义特指“自主移动机器人、人形机器人和四足机器人”，它们可以四处移动、避开障碍物、重量为 4.4 磅或以上，包括任何地面站或对接站。 许多机器人吸尘器和割草机都符合这些标准，FCC 已向 PC Mag 确认该禁令确实适用于清洁机器人。

这对于科沃斯、石头、Dreame等大型机器人品牌来说是个坏消息；美国排名前五的扫地机器人品牌均为中国品牌，因此属于此次禁令的范围，因此我们联系了他们征求意见。

Anker Innovations（Eufy 母公司）首席通信官 Eric Villines 告诉 TechRadar：“我们了解 FCC 的最新更新。” “根据我们目前的了解，新规则不会影响我们目前在美国销售的产品的持续可用性、使用或支持。 这些产品仍然可用，并将继续获得更新和客户支持，

订阅突发新闻、评论、观点、顶级技术交易等。

“与业内其他公司一样，我们正在寻求进一步明确该规则将如何应用于未来的产品，并且我们将随时向客户通报情况。 我们仍然致力于遵守我们经营所在每个市场的所有监管要求。”

其他几个智能家居品牌在早期阶段拒绝发表评论，但我们普遍认为这一消息可能有点令人意外。

您可以继续使用您的 robovac 吗？

然而，乌云中也有一丝阳光：该禁令不具有追溯力，因此，如果机器人已经获得 FCC 授权在美国销售，那就没问题了。 该禁令并不阻止零售商“继续销售、进口或营销之前批准的相关型号”。

尽管如此，PC Mag 还确定了一项单独的 FCC 命令，其中规定现有的机器人吸尘器和类似产品“至少在 2029 年 1 月 1 日之前可能会继续接收软件和固件更新，以减轻对美国消费者的伤害”。 如果联邦通信委员会决定不延长这一期限，那么它只会对在美国销售的任何新的中国制造的扫地机器人设置一个倒计时。

对于受影响的制造商来说，下一步将是游说FCC，希望为其部分或全部产品获得豁免：毕竟，自动驾驶、自清洁拖把和能够携带AR-15的机器狗之间存在很大差异。 然而，到目前为止，中国主要无人机或路由器制造商尚未获得任何豁免，因此受影响公司的未来看起来并不光明。
